info.desc: Dog Man Star is the second album by English alternative rock band Suede, released in October 1994 on Nude Records. It was the last Suede album to feature guitarist Bernard Butler, due to growing tensions between Butler and singer Brett Anderson ending with Butler leaving the band before the album was completed. Dog Man Star is more downbeat than their debut and chronicles Suede as they parted from the "Britpop pack". Although it did not sell on the same scale as their chart-topping debut Suede (1993), Dog Man Star reached number three on the UK Albums Chart. Released to a .

podcast.body: Released rapidly after their debut, this album represented a "second revolution" for the band, featuring more lineup changes. It was described as a "completely revolutionary act" because Suede intentionally defied the formula that brought them initial success, opting for a much darker, deeper, and intimate sound with "very minority and sometimes scandalous lyrics." Despite not achieving the sales peak of its predecessor, it was critically adored, considered "one of the master albums of the 90s." The band aimed to avoid being a "mass consumption object," aspiring to the artistic depth of David Bowie's Berlin Trilogy rather than the mass appeal of Ziggy Stardust. The recording process was complicated by the mysterious departure of Bernard Butler, a key musical figure from their first album, and issues with producer Ed Buller. The band remained very proud of the result, which is now considered a masterpiece. "hacen un salto enormemente arrisgado y se revelan contra todo lo que en principio les iba a dar éxito."

Suede's second album, released in 1994, is cited as an example of a band's stylistic evolution within the Britpop era. It showcased a move towards a more "intellectual" and "glam" direction, following a strong debut. "después he ido al dogma estar intelectual."
